chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Bureyd al-Ajli from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who has a slave girl under him, so he divorces her with two divorces, then buys her afterwards. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to marry her until she marries another husband, and until he enters with her in a manner similar to what she went out from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who divorces his slave girl and then buys her back?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific mechanics of 'Iddah' and remarriage for a slave woman divorced twice, requiring a genuine intervening marriage (Nikah) with consummation to restore her status, mirroring the rule for free women. It highlights the juristic distinction between simple repurchase and the necessity of a new contractual bond, ensuring the divorce is fully effective before reintegration. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the nuances of manumission and marital rights within the household structure.
